messages:
maya: quick sanity check — after the v3 FlashAttention integration i'm seeing a weird p99 jump for small batch sizes (b=1..4) on T4s. not full OOMs but latency spikes + occasional kernel fallback logs. anyone else?
sanjay: seen it on a single customer repro yesterday, thanks for raising. rough numbers?
maya: baseline (fa2) on same hw: 8 tokens/s @ b=1, p99 ~ 120ms. fa3 build: 5 tokens/s @ b=1, p99 ~ 420ms. b=8 is fine.
eli: do you have the kernel-fallback trace? runtime logs should show when we switch from flash kernel -> generic matmul.
maya: pasted logs below: ```
[2026-03-18T14:22:03Z] kernel_select: selected flashv3_k128 for seq=16,bs=1
[2026-03-18T14:22:03Z] kernel_exec: cudnn fallback triggered: workspace alloc failed 134217728 bytes
[2026-03-18T14:22:03Z] kernel_select: fallback to generic_attn (slow path)
```
eli: workspace alloc failed — that explains the fallback. flashv3_kernel attempts a workspace that doesn't fit at small batch sizes because of pad-to-block heuristics.
eli: our heuristics assume batching will amortize workspace; small bs + some padding leads to unexpectedly large per-request workspace.
ari? (typo: aaron)
aaron: i can repro locally with a minimal script. will run nvprof and check peak device mem and fragmentation.
perf-bot: benchmark job started: job_id=fb3-small-bsz-1912345678, nodes=1,t4x1,model=gpt-medium,requests=1000
sanjay: possible short-term mitigation: lower flash kernel workspace cap for single-request paths and prefer a smaller kernel tile (k64) for seq<=32 and bs<=4. long-term we should add a per-stream mem-reservation check before selecting high-workspace kernels.
maya: +1. are there perf regressions for med/large bs if we force k64?
eli: forcing k64 reduces max throughput ~6% at bs=32, seq=64 on A100 in our microbench, but removes the p99 spike for small bs. tradeoff looks acceptable for customer-facing SLO.
aaron: nvprof dump: fragmentation is the culprit — the allocator hands back tiny free blocks, and flashv3 tries a single large cudaMalloc. also saw some leftover KV cache allocations from previous requests on the same stream.
sanjay: two engineering proposals: 1) runtime heuristic change: if bs<=4 && seq<=48 prefer low-ws kernels, set per-request workspace cap 64MB. 2) allocator change: provide temporary pinned buffer pool to satisfy large contiguous workspace requests to avoid fragmentation-induced fallbacks.
maya: i'd prioritize #1 + telemetry (how often we fallback). #2 is bigger but could help high-concurrency cases.
eli: agree. telemetry: add metric flash/kernel_fallback{reason=workspace, kernel=flashv3_k128} and record peak_worst_free_bytes at selection time.
aaron: i'll attach profiler and a minimal repro in the ticket. also want a CI microbenchmark that runs b in [1,2,4,8] and asserts p99 < 200ms.
sanjay: note: we need to keep model quality parity — some models rely on k128 for numerical stability; add a model whitelist for forced larger-k kernels.
maya: ok next actions: aaron create ticket + attach nvprof (ETA today), eli will draft heuristic patch and add telemetry (ETA tomorrow), sanjay will bake perf CI check into infra (ETA this week). i'll notify on rollout plan after we run perf job. :thumbsup:
perf-bot: job fb3-small-bsz-1912345678 completed: median latency 85ms, p99 190ms, no fallbacks observed. artifacts: s3://redwood-perf/fb3-small-bsz-1912345678/
eli: awesome, looks like the heuristic fix works on that infra. we'll still validate on multi-tenant stacks.
aaron: uploaded repro + nvprof to the ticket: https://internal/redwood/issue/RI-4321
maya: thanks all. will follow up if customer sees anything else. :pray:
